overview.title: Common types of personal injury cases we handle in Houston.
overview.text: We don't back down when accountability is on the line — and we have the track record to prove it, including results against national corporations, global manufacturers and insurance giants; but what drives us is the opportunity to help people regain stability and a sense of control during uncertain times.

services.title: Car Accidents
services.summary: Freeway pileups, intersection and DWI crashes
services.text: From freeway pileups on the 610 Loop to crush-injury crashes on I-10. Texas law gives you the right to recover compensation for your medical bills, lost income, and pain and suffering, but that recovery does not happen automatically.
services.lead: You were just in a car accident. The shock is wearing off, the pain is starting to set in, and now your phone is ringing — the other driver's insurance company wants a statement. Before you say a word to them, here is what you need to know: Texas law gives you the right to recover compensation for your medical bills, lost income, and pain and suffering. But that recovery does not happen automatically, and the insurance company on the other end of that phone is not on your side.

covers.title: Rear-End Collisions
covers.text: The rear driver is presumed at fault in most Texas rear-end cases under the duty to maintain a safe following distance. Insurers often dispute injury severity, especially when vehicle damage looks minor.

covers.title: T-Bone and Intersection Collisions
covers.text: Fault usually turns on who had the right of way and whether either driver ran a light or sign. Eyewitness testimony, traffic camera footage and event data recorder data are critical.

covers.title: Head-On Collisions
covers.text: Often the most catastrophic crashes, frequently involving impaired drivers, wrong-way drivers, or drivers who crossed the center line.

covers.title: Multi-Vehicle Pileups
covers.text: Liability may be shared across several drivers, and Texas's modified comparative fault rule complicates recovery. These cases require careful crash reconstruction.

covers.title: Hit-and-Run Crashes
covers.text: When the at-fault driver flees and cannot be identified, recovery typically depends on your own uninsured motorist coverage.

covers.title: Drunk Driving Crashes
covers.text: DWI crashes open the door to punitive damages for gross negligence and may also trigger Dram Shop Act liability against bars or restaurants that overserved the driver.

questions.q: What if I was partially to blame for the crash?
questions.a: Texas's modified comparative fault rule lets you recover as long as you are 50% or less at fault, and your award is reduced by your percentage of fault. Do not assume partial fault disqualifies you.

questions.q: How long do I have to file?
questions.a: Texas gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. Claims against government entities have shorter notice deadlines, sometimes as short as six months.

questions.q: What does it cost to hire you?
questions.a: Our car accident cases are handled on a contingency fee basis — no upfront cost, no hourly billing, and no out-of-pocket expense for case investigation, expert witnesses or filing fees. If we do not recover compensation, you owe us nothing.

services.title: Trucking Accidents
services.text: Houston is one of the nation's busiest port cities — big rigs are everywhere. Truck accidents are not regular car accidents, and the investigation has already started by the trucking company, not for you.
services.lead: You were just hit by an 18-wheeler, an oilfield rig, a delivery truck, or a commercial vehicle. Maybe you survived. Maybe a family member did not. Either way, the trucking company already has investigators on the ground, a defense team in motion, and one job: limit what they pay. Texas truck accident law gives you the right to hold the driver, the trucking company and every other responsible party accountable.

covers.title: The Rapid Response Team
covers.text: Within hours of the crash the trucking company dispatches lawyers, investigators, accident reconstructionists and adjusters to the scene — all working to build a defense.

covers.title: Electronic Evidence
covers.text: Electronic logging device data, dashcam footage and GPS records are preserved selectively. What hurts the trucking company tends to disappear if a preservation letter does not arrive in time.

covers.title: The Vehicle Itself
covers.text: The truck may already be back on the road, repaired or scrapped, destroying critical physical evidence.

covers.title: Driver and Company Records
covers.text: The driver's qualification file, training records and prior violations are reviewed internally for damage control before anyone else sees them.

services.title: Wrongful Death
services.summary: Claims for families who lost a loved one
services.text: Texas wrongful death law gives surviving families specific rights under two separate statutes: the Texas Wrongful Death Act for what the family lost, and the Survival Action statute for what the deceased lost between injury and death.
services.lead: Your loved one is gone — and the cause was someone else's negligence. Maybe a drunk driver, a distracted truck driver, a careless surgeon, a defective product, an untrained boat operator, an unsafe property. The grief is unbearable, and on top of that you are now facing funeral bills, lost income, and a future without the person who held your family together. The two Texas claims work together; pursued by a firm that does not understand the framework, valid recoveries get left on the table.

covers.title: The Texas Wrongful Death Act
covers.text: The claim that compensates surviving family members for what the family lost when their loved one died.

covers.title: The Survival Action Statute
covers.text: A separate claim for what the deceased lost between the injury and the death. Pursued correctly alongside the wrongful death claim, the two can deliver full justice.

covers.title: Early Insurer Contact
covers.text: The defendant's carrier often reaches out within days of the death with sympathetic-sounding offers designed to close the case before you have consulted a lawyer.

covers.title: Evidence and Witnesses
covers.text: Police reports, medical records, surveillance footage and employment records are being secured by the defense. Witnesses scatter, and memories fade.

services.title: Motorcycle Accidents
services.summary: Rider claims and the bias that follows them
services.text: Especially around downtown nightlife districts and along the Gulf Freeway. Texas law gives motorcyclists the same right to recover compensation as any other accident victim. The problem is not the law — it is the bias.
services.lead: You were riding legally, paying attention, and doing everything right when another driver pulled out, turned left, changed lanes, or did not see you. Now you are dealing with serious injuries, and the other driver's insurance company is already preparing to blame you for the crash. Insurance adjusters, defense lawyers and even some jurors carry stereotypes about riders that drive down settlements before the facts are even examined.

covers.title: The Default Narrative
covers.text: The other driver's adjuster is already framing the crash as rider fault, regardless of what actually happened.

covers.title: Where Investigators Look
covers.text: They examine your gear, your bike and your speed rather than the other driver's failure to yield, look, or stay in their lane.

covers.title: The Police Report
covers.text: Officers on scene sometimes default to assumptions about motorcyclists that show up in the report's narrative section before your version is heard.

covers.title: Witness Memory
covers.text: Witnesses' memories degrade by the hour, and most people who saw the whole thing do not see what they think they did.

services.title: Workplace Accidents
services.text: Frequent in booming Houston job centers and industrial corridors. Texas is the only state where workers' compensation is optional for private employers, and that single fact changes everything about your case.
services.lead: You got hurt on the job. Now your employer is telling you about workers' comp, or they are saying you do not qualify, or they are handing you a stack of paperwork to sign. If your employer does not carry workers' comp — a non-subscriber — or if a third party caused your injury, you may have the right to file a full personal injury lawsuit rather than a capped workers' comp claim. The damages available are dramatically higher.

covers.title: Pathway 1 — Your Employer Has Workers' Comp
covers.text: If your employer carries Texas workers' compensation insurance you are generally limited to workers' comp benefits, and you typically cannot sue them directly under Texas Labor Code 408.001. Workers' comp does not cover pain and suffering, mental anguish, or full lost earning capacity.

covers.title: Pathway 2 — Your Employer Is a Non-Subscriber
covers.text: If your employer opted out of the workers' comp system under Texas Labor Code Chapter 406, you can sue them directly in a personal injury lawsuit, and Texas Labor Code 406.033 gives you significant strategic advantages.

covers.title: Pathway 3 — A Third Party Caused the Injury
covers.text: Where someone other than your employer caused the harm, a claim against that party sits outside the workers' comp system and carries the full range of personal injury damages.

services.title: Pedestrian Accidents
services.summary: Struck while walking, and blamed for it
services.text: Texas law gives pedestrians strong protections, including a driver's affirmative duty under Texas Transportation Code 552.008 to exercise due care to avoid pedestrians on the roadway, regardless of where the pedestrian is.
services.lead: You were walking — to your car, across the street, on a sidewalk, in a parking lot — and a driver hit you. Now you are in the hospital, or worse, a family member is. The driver's insurance company is already preparing to argue you stepped out, you were not paying attention, you were not in a crosswalk, you were wearing dark clothes. None of those arguments end your case.

covers.title: Pedestrian Blame
covers.text: The driver's adjuster frames the crash as your fault. Pedestrian blame is the default defense in nearly every Texas pedestrian claim, regardless of the circumstances.

covers.title: Disappearing Scene Evidence
covers.text: Skid marks, debris fields and visibility conditions documented at the scene tell a different story than a police report written two days later.

covers.title: The Report's Wording
covers.text: A report that says you were outside the crosswalk or stepped out suddenly gets repeated for years, even when video, witness statements or physics contradict it.

covers.title: Camera Footage
covers.text: Surveillance and traffic camera footage is overwritten within days at most retail and intersection cameras, often before victims leave the hospital.

services.title: Premises Liability
services.text: Texas premises liability law turns on a threshold question most claimants do not know exists: were you legally an invitee, a licensee or a trespasser? The answer determines what duty the property owner owed you.
services.lead: You were injured on someone else's property — a store, an apartment complex, a restaurant, a parking lot, a hotel, a workplace. The injury was not your fault. The property owner had a legal duty to keep the premises safe, and they failed. Now you are dealing with medical bills, lost wages, and an insurance company already preparing to argue you should have seen the danger, you were trespassing, or the condition was open and obvious.

covers.title: Your Legal Status
covers.text: The property owner's adjuster asks why you were on the property and what you were doing, because the answers determine whether they owe you anything at all under Texas law.

covers.title: Surveillance Footage
covers.text: Most retail and apartment surveillance is overwritten within 7 to 30 days. Footage showing the hazard before your fall, prior incidents, or when the spill occurred often disappears unless a preservation letter arrives fast.

covers.title: Incident Reports
covers.text: Many incident reports are written by managers trained to document only what protects the business, not what actually happened.

covers.title: Maintenance and Inspection Logs
covers.text: Records showing the owner knew about the hazard before your injury are some of the most valuable evidence in any premises case, and the most likely to go missing.

services.title: Maritime & Offshore Accidents
services.summary: Jones Act, LHWCA, OCSLA and DOHSA claims
services.text: An offshore injury case is not a single category. It is at least four legal pathways, and which one applies changes what you can recover and how long you have to file.
services.lead: You were injured offshore — on an oil rig, a crew boat, a barge, a tanker, a fishing vessel, a dock or a shipyard. Your case is at least four categories: the Jones Act for seamen, LHWCA for harbor and dock workers, OCSLA for fixed platforms, and DOHSA for families of workers killed more than three nautical miles offshore. Get this wrong and you can end up with the wrong claim filed in the wrong forum past the wrong deadline. We help injured Texas maritime workers identify the right pathway, build the right case, and, when complexity demands it, partner with the maritime specialists who can take the case the rest of the way.

covers.title: How Your Employer Classifies You
covers.text: Companies frequently classify injured workers as non-seamen to push them into LHWCA or state workers' compensation rather than the Jones Act, where damages are far higher.

covers.title: The Company Doctor
covers.text: Maintenance and cure benefits are paid by the employer, who has a direct financial interest in minimizing your injury severity. The first medical reports almost always favor the company.

covers.title: Vessel Records
covers.text: Vessel logs, accident reports, JSA forms and safety meeting minutes are collected selectively, and documents that hurt the employer have a way of becoming hard to find.

covers.title: Crew Witnesses
covers.text: Crew rotations move offshore workers to different vessels, different jobs and sometimes different states. By the time you find them, memories are unreliable and loyalties have shifted.

services.title: Aviation Accidents
services.summary: Crash claims for passengers, crew and families
services.text: These cases involve federal aviation law, Texas personal injury law and often product liability, and they require accident reconstruction experts, NTSB report analysis and litigation against well-funded airlines, manufacturers and insurers.
services.lead: A Texas aviation accident lawyer represents pilots, passengers, crew and surviving family members in civil claims after aircraft crashes. If you or a loved one was hurt or killed in an aviation crash, our team is ready to investigate, file your claim and pursue the full compensation you deserve. Under federal law, the National Transportation Safety Board investigates all civil aviation accidents in the United States.

covers.title: Commercial Airline Crashes
covers.text: Claims against scheduled carriers, where federal aviation law and Texas personal injury law both apply.

covers.title: Private and Chartered Plane Crashes
covers.text: Cases involving private owners, charter operators and the maintenance and training records behind the flight.

covers.title: Helicopter Crashes
covers.text: Including medevac and offshore transport flights, each with its own operators and legal framework.

covers.title: Corporate Jets, Air Taxis and Tour Flights
covers.text: Corporate jet accidents and air taxi or tour flight incidents, where the operator's status shapes the claim.

covers.title: Agricultural Aviation and Ground Incidents
covers.text: Crop duster crashes, runway collisions and ground incidents involving aircraft.

services.title: Product Liability
services.summary: Defective vehicles, drugs and medical devices
services.text: Under Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code Chapter 82, you can hold manufacturers, distributors and sellers accountable for design defects, manufacturing defects and inadequate warnings.
services.lead: You used a product the way it was meant to be used — and it hurt you. A vehicle safety system failed. A prescription drug caused harm the manufacturer did not warn about. A medical device implanted to help you ended up making things worse. Texas law gives consumers powerful rights against manufacturers, distributors and sellers who put dangerous products into the marketplace.

covers.title: A National Defense Team
covers.text: The manufacturer has a defense team that has handled hundreds of similar claims and knows exactly how to limit liability.

covers.title: The Missing Product
covers.text: Hospitals dispose of defective medical devices, body shops scrap crashed vehicles, and pharmacies do not keep returned medications. Once the product is gone, proving the defect becomes much harder.

covers.title: Scattered Records
covers.text: Recalls, warnings and prior incidents sit across the manufacturer's files, FDA databases, NHTSA records and consumer complaint logs. Building the pattern requires deep regulatory investigation.

covers.title: Sellers and Distributors
covers.text: Texas law under section 82.003 generally protects non-manufacturing sellers, but with critical exceptions worth pursuing in the right cases.

services.text: Cyclists face unique dangers on Houston roads. We stand up for injured riders hit by careless motorists, unsafe road design, or negligent commercial drivers.

about.title: About Amaro Law Firm
text: With offices across Texas and a reputation for powerful representation, Amaro Law Firm has been going toe-to-toe with insurance companies, major corporations and negligent parties since its founding in 2005. But we're here for more than legal strategy. We're here to listen, to explain your options in plain language, and to help you make decisions that honor what you've been through.

Our mission is simple but powerful: to guide injury survivors with clarity, compassion, and the courage to pursue accountability when it matters most. For over two decades, we've stood shoulder-to-shoulder with clients who are facing some of the toughest challenges of their lives following serious injury and loss.

We are Justice Driven, and we believe that every person deserves a law firm that stands with them, explains what comes next in plain language, and fights for accountability without losing sight of their humanity. We don't just handle personal injury claims; we help people navigate life after an injury with the information, support and advocacy they need to move forward.

The heart of our firm begins with our founder, James Amaro. A graduate of the University of Texas at Austin and a J.D. recipient from the University of Houston Law Center, Mr. Amaro began his career representing some of the largest insurance companies in Texas. After witnessing firsthand how everyday people were mistreated or ignored during times of crisis, he made a career-defining pivot: to stand with the people whose voices weren't being heard.

While our firm handles a wide range of personal injury and commercial litigation matters, we're known for our depth in catastrophic injury claims, truck and motor vehicle accidents, defective products and wrongful death suits. Every client matters. Every case matters. And every person we work with deserves to feel seen, heard and supported.

faqs.a: Yes. We never charge for consultations, and you only pay if we win your case.

faqs.q: Do I have to come to the office?
faqs.a: No. We make the process as convenient as possible — you can speak with us over the phone, by video, or online. If needed, we can also come to you.

faqs.q: How fast will someone contact me?
faqs.a: We understand your situation is urgent. Our team typically responds quickly, often the same day, to discuss your case and next steps.

faqs.q: Why should I contact Amaro Law Firm now?
faqs.a: Acting quickly can make a big difference in your case. Evidence can fade and deadlines may apply, so contacting us now helps protect your rights.

faqs.q: What should I do after a car accident in Houston?
faqs.a: After a crash in Houston, your first priority is safety. Call 911, seek medical care, and request a police report from HPD or the responding agency. Houston traffic accidents often involve multiple vehicles or commercial drivers, so it's important not to speak with insurance adjusters before talking to a lawyer.

faqs.q: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Houston, Texas?
faqs.a: In most Houston personal injury cases, Texas law gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a claim. However, cases involving government vehicles, dangerous road conditions, or public property may have much shorter deadlines.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to court for a personal injury case in Houston?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Many Houston injury cases settle without going to trial. That said, insurance companies know which firms are willing to take cases to Harris County civil court if needed.

faqs.q: How much is my Houston personal injury case worth?
faqs.a: Every case is different. The value depends on factors like medical costs, lost wages, pain and suffering, and how the injury affects your daily life.

faqs.q: What types of accidents are most common in Houston injury cases?
faqs.a: Houston sees a high number of car and truck accidents on I-45, I-10 and the 610 Loop; 18-wheeler and commercial vehicle crashes tied to port and refinery traffic; workplace and construction accidents in industrial corridors; and motorcycle accidents near downtown and major nightlife districts. These cases often involve complex insurance and liability issues.
